reason: The text demonstrates agency by numerous non-leader figures and groups throughout the narrative. The tribes of Israel collectively initiate action and speak to David before his anointing (וַיָּבֹאוּ כָּל־ שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל). The text repeatedly refers to 'all the people' (כל־ הָעָם) as active agents: playing instruments before the Lord, transporting the Ark, receiving portions, and returning to their homes (וַיְחַלֵּק לְכָל־ הָעָם). Non-leader individuals like Uzzah (a servant) perform actions independently, and even Obed-edom (a Gittite) receives blessings. The Philistines also act as independent agents in response to events. While David is portrayed as the central leader, the narrative consistently depicts agency across multiple levels of society—collective tribal action, common people, servants, and individuals. The statement overgeneralizes by restricting agency exclusively to leaders.
